inputs.text: Mahama is right: law should grow from a nation’s traditions and the consent of its people, not be imposed by fashionable global debates. Leaders swear to uphold the law, not to set aside public judgment in favor of outside pressure. When law loses touch with family life and inherited values, trust and social order suffer. A country’s people—not distant cultural trends—must have the final say.
